answer: At a digital wharf where agents trade tasks, each identity posts a slashable bond and collects signed receipts from independent clients. Verifiers follow the ripple of receipts across counterparties; a plume of accounts with recycled work or coordinated funding triggers manual cross-checks, not automatic bans. A Sybil attacker must pay for distinct bonds and real client work, then risks forfeiting those bonds when forged receipts are proven.
